answer: SELECT T1.title FROM albums AS T1 JOIN tracks AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.album_id GROUP BY T1.id HAVING count(T1.id)  >  10;

CREATE TABLE `Customers` (
  `customer_id` NUMBER,
  `customer_first_name` TEXT,
  `customer_middle_initial` TEXT,
  `customer_last_name` TEXT,
  `gender` TEXT,
  `email_address` TEXT,
  `login_name` TEXT,
  `login_password` TEXT,
  `phone_number` TEXT,
  `town_city` TEXT,
  `state_county_province` TEXT,
  `country` TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (`customer_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `Orders` (
  `order_id` NUMBER,
  `customer_id` NUMBER REFERENCES `Customers`(`customer_id`),
  `date_order_placed` TIME,
  `order_details` TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (`order_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `Invoices` (
  `invoice_number` NUMBER,
  `order_id` NUMBER REFERENCES `Orders`(`order_id`),
  `invoice_date` TIME,
  PRIMARY KEY (`invoice_number`)
);

CREATE TABLE `Accounts` (
  `account_id` NUMBER,
  `customer_id` NUMBER REFERENCES `Customers`(`customer_id`),
  `date_account_opened` TIME,
  `account_name` TEXT,
  `other_account_details` TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (`account_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `Product_Categories` (
  `production_type_code` TEXT,
  `product_type_description` TEXT,
  `vat_rating` NUMBER,
  PRIMARY KEY (`production_type_code`)
);

CREATE TABLE `Products` (
  `product_id` NUMBER,
  `parent_product_id` NUMBER,
  `production_type_code` TEXT REFERENCES `Product_Categories`(`production_type_code`),
  `unit_price` NUMBER,
  `product_name` TEXT,
  `product_color` TEXT,
  `product_size` TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (`product_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `Financial_Transactions` (
  `transaction_id` NUMBER,
  `account_id` NUMBER REFERENCES `Accounts`(`account_id`),
  `invoice_number` NUMBER REFERENCES `Invoices`(`invoice_number`),
  `transaction_type` TEXT,
  `transaction_date` TIME,
  `transaction_amount` NUMBER,
  `transaction_comment` TEXT,
  `other_transaction_details` TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE `Order_Items` (
  `order_item_id` NUMBER,
  `order_id` NUMBER REFERENCES `Orders`(`order_id`),
  `product_id` NUMBER REFERENCES `Products`(`product_id`),
  `product_quantity` TEXT,
  `other_order_item_details` TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (`order_item_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `Invoice_Line_Items` (
  `order_item_id` NUMBER REFERENCES `Order_Items`(`order_item_id`),
  `invoice_number` NUMBER REFERENCES `Invoices`(`invoice_number`),
  `product_id` NUMBER REFERENCES `Products`(`product_id`),
  `product_title` TEXT,
  `product_quantity` TEXT,
  `product_price` NUMBER,
  `derived_product_cost` NUMBER,
  `derived_vat_payable` NUMBER,
  `derived_total_cost` NUMBER
);

Question:
Show the id, the account name, and other account details for all accounts by the customer with first name 'Meaghan'.
answer: SELECT T1.account_id ,  T1.date_account_opened ,  T1.account_name ,  T1.other_account_details FROM Accounts AS T1 JOIN Customers AS T2 ON T1.customer_id  =  T2.customer_id WHERE T2.customer_first_name  =  'Meaghan'

CREATE TABLE `circuits` (
  `circuitId` NUMBER,
  `circuitRef` TEXT,
  `name` TEXT,
  `location` TEXT,
  `country` TEXT,
  `lat` NUMBER,
  `lng` NUMBER,
  `alt` NUMBER,
  `url` TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (`circuitId`)
);

CREATE TABLE `races` (
  `raceId` NUMBER,
  `year` NUMBER,
  `round` NUMBER,
  `circuitId` NUMBER REFERENCES `circuits`(`circuitId`),
  `name` TEXT,
  `date` TEXT,
  `time` TEXT,
  `url` TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (`raceId`)
);

CREATE TABLE `drivers` (
  `driverId` NUMBER,
  `driverRef` TEXT,
  `number` NUMBER,
  `code` TEXT,
  `forename` TEXT,
  `surname` TEXT,
  `dob` TEXT,
  `nationality` TEXT,
  `url` TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (`driverId`)
);

CREATE TABLE `status` (
  `statusId` NUMBER,
  `status` TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (`statusId`)
);

CREATE TABLE `seasons` (
  `year` NUMBER,
  `url` TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (`year`)
);

CREATE TABLE `constructors` (
  `constructorId` NUMBER,
  `constructorRef` TEXT,
  `name` TEXT,
  `nationality` TEXT,
  `url` TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (`constructorId`)
);

CREATE TABLE `constructorStandings` (
  `constructorStandingsId` NUMBER,
  `raceId` NUMBER REFERENCES `races`(`raceId`),
  `constructorId` NUMBER REFERENCES `constructors`(`constructorId`),
  `points` NUMBER,
  `position` NUMBER,
  `positionText` TEXT,
  `wins` NUMBER,
  PRIMARY KEY (`constructorStandingsId`)
);

CREATE TABLE `results` (
  `resultId` NUMBER,
  `raceId` NUMBER REFERENCES `races`(`raceId`),
  `driverId` NUMBER REFERENCES `drivers`(`driverId`),
  `constructorId` NUMBER REFERENCES `constructors`(`constructorId`),
  `number` NUMBER,
  `grid` NUMBER,
  `position` NUMBER,
  `positionText` TEXT,
  `positionOrder` NUMBER,
  `points` NUMBER,
  `laps` NUMBER,
  `time` TEXT,
  `milliseconds` NUMBER,
  `fastestLap` NUMBER,
  `rank` NUMBER,
  `fastestLapTime` TEXT,
  `fastestLapSpeed` TEXT,
  `statusId` NUMBER,
  PRIMARY KEY (`resultId`)
);

CREATE TABLE `driverStandings` (
  `driverStandingsId` NUMBER,
  `raceId` NUMBER REFERENCES `races`(`raceId`),
  `driverId` NUMBER REFERENCES `drivers`(`driverId`),
  `points` NUMBER,
  `position` NUMBER,
  `positionText` TEXT,
  `wins` NUMBER,
  PRIMARY KEY (`driverStandingsId`)
);

CREATE TABLE `constructorResults` (
  `constructorResultsId` NUMBER,
  `raceId` NUMBER REFERENCES `races`(`raceId`),
  `constructorId` NUMBER REFERENCES `constructors`(`constructorId`),
  `points` NUMBER,
  `status` NUMBER,
  PRIMARY KEY (`constructorResultsId`)
);

CREATE TABLE `qualifying` (
  `qualifyId` NUMBER,
  `raceId` NUMBER REFERENCES `races`(`raceId`),
  `driverId` NUMBER REFERENCES `drivers`(`driverId`),
  `constructorId` NUMBER REFERENCES `constructors`(`constructorId`),
  `number` NUMBER,
  `position` NUMBER,
  `q1` TEXT,
  `q2` TEXT,
  `q3` TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (`qualifyId`)
);

CREATE TABLE `pitStops` (
  `raceId` NUMBER REFERENCES `races`(`raceId`),
  `driverId` NUMBER REFERENCES `drivers`(`driverId`),
  `stop` NUMBER,
  `lap` NUMBER,
  `time` TEXT,
  `duration` TEXT,
  `milliseconds` NUMBER,
  PRIMARY KEY (`raceId`)
);

CREATE TABLE `lapTimes` (
  `raceId` NUMBER REFERENCES `races`(`raceId`),
  `driverId` NUMBER REFERENCES `drivers`(`driverId`),
  `lap` NUMBER,
  `position` NUMBER,
  `time` TEXT,
  `milliseconds` NUMBER,
  PRIMARY KEY (`raceId`)
);

Question:
What are the ids and last names of all drivers who participated in the most races?
answer: SELECT T1.driverid ,  T1.surname FROM drivers AS T1 JOIN results AS T2 ON T1.driverid = T2.driverid JOIN races AS T3 ON T2.raceid = T3.raceid GROUP BY T1.driverid ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1

Database Schema:
CREATE TABLE `Campuses` (
  `Id` NUMBER,
  `Campus` TEXT,
  `Location` TEXT,
  `County` TEXT,
  `Year` NUMBER,
  PRIMARY KEY (`Id`)
);

  `Campus` NUMBER REFERENCES `Campuses`(`Id`),

  PRIMARY KEY (`Campus`)
);

CREATE TABLE `degrees` (
  `Year` NUMBER,
  `Campus` NUMBER REFERENCES `Campuses`(`Id`),
  `Degrees` NUMBER,
  PRIMARY KEY (`Year`)
);

CREATE TABLE `discipline_enrollments` (
  `Campus` NUMBER REFERENCES `Campuses`(`Id`),
  `Discipline` NUMBER,
  `Year` NUMBER,
  `Undergraduate` NUMBER,
  `Graduate` NUMBER,
  PRIMARY KEY (`Campus`)
);

CREATE TABLE `enrollments` (
  `Campus` NUMBER REFERENCES `Campuses`(`Id`),
  `Year` NUMBER,
  `TotalEnrollment_AY` NUMBER,
  `FTE_AY` NUMBER,
  PRIMARY KEY (`Campus`)
);

CREATE TABLE `faculty` (
  `Campus` NUMBER REFERENCES `Campuses`(`Id`),
  `Year` NUMBER,
  `Faculty` NUMBER
);

Question:
What campus has the most degrees  conferrred over its entire existence?
answer: SELECT campus FROM degrees GROUP BY campus ORDER BY sum(degrees) DESC LIMIT 1

Question:
Who has written a paper that has the word "Functional" in its title? Return the first names of the authors.
answer: SELECT t1.fname FROM authors AS t1 JOIN authorship AS t2 ON t1.authid  =  t2.authid JOIN papers AS t3 ON t2.paperid  =  t3.paperid WHERE t3.title LIKE "%Functional%"

);

);

CREATE TABLE `payment` (

Question:
Which part fault requires the most number of skills to fix? List part id and name.
answer: SELECT T1.part_id ,  T1.part_name FROM Parts AS T1 JOIN Part_Faults AS T2 ON T1.part_id  =  T2.part_id JOIN Skills_Required_To_Fix AS T3 ON T2.part_fault_id  =  T3.part_fault_id GROUP BY T1.part_id ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1

  `Club_ID` NUMBER,
  `name` TEXT,
  `Region` TEXT,
  `Start_year` TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (`Club_ID`)
);

CREATE TABLE `club_rank` (
  `Rank` NUMBER,
  `Club_ID` NUMBER REFERENCES `club`(`Club_ID`),
  `Gold` NUMBER,
  `Silver` NUMBER,
  `Bronze` NUMBER,
  `Total` NUMBER,
  PRIMARY KEY (`Rank`)
);

CREATE TABLE `player` (
  `Player_ID` NUMBER,
  `name` TEXT,
  `Position` TEXT,
  `Club_ID` NUMBER REFERENCES `club`(`Club_ID`),
  `Apps` NUMBER,
  `Tries` NUMBER,
  `Goals` TEXT,
  `Points` NUMBER,
  PRIMARY KEY (`Player_ID`)
);

CREATE TABLE `competition` (
  `Competition_ID` NUMBER,
  `Year` NUMBER,
  `Competition_type` TEXT,
  `Country` TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (`Competition_ID`)
);

CREATE TABLE `competition_result` (
  `Competition_ID` NUMBER REFERENCES `competition`(`Competition_ID`),
  `Club_ID_1` NUMBER REFERENCES `club`(`Club_ID`),
  `Club_ID_2` NUMBER REFERENCES `club`(`Club_ID`),
  `Score` TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (`Competition_ID`)
);

Question:
List the most common type of competition.
answer: SELECT Competition_type FROM competition GROUP BY Competition_type ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

  `REGION_ID` NUMBER,
  `REGION_NAME` TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (`REGION_ID`)
);

CREATE TABLE `countries` (
  `COUNTRY_ID` TEXT,
  `COUNTRY_NAME` TEXT,
  `REGION_ID` NUMBER REFERENCES `regions`(`REGION_ID`),
  PRIMARY KEY (`COUNTRY_ID`)
);

CREATE TABLE `departments` (
  `DEPARTMENT_ID` NUMBER,
  `DEPARTMENT_NAME` TEXT,
  `MANAGER_ID` NUMBER,
  `LOCATION_ID` NUMBER,
  PRIMARY KEY (`DEPARTMENT_ID`)
);

CREATE TABLE `jobs` (
  `JOB_ID` TEXT,
  `JOB_TITLE` TEXT,
  `MIN_SALARY` NUMBER,
  `MAX_SALARY` NUMBER,
  PRIMARY KEY (`JOB_ID`)
);

CREATE TABLE `employees` (
  `EMPLOYEE_ID` NUMBER,
  `FIRST_NAME` TEXT,
  `LAST_NAME` TEXT,
  `EMAIL` TEXT,
  `PHONE_NUMBER` TEXT,
  `HIRE_DATE` TIME,
  `JOB_ID` TEXT REFERENCES `jobs`(`JOB_ID`),
  `SALARY` NUMBER,
  `COMMISSION_PCT` NUMBER,
  `MANAGER_ID` NUMBER,
  `DEPARTMENT_ID` NUMBER REFERENCES `departments`(`DEPARTMENT_ID`),
  PRIMARY KEY (`EMPLOYEE_ID`)
);

CREATE TABLE `job_history` (
  `EMPLOYEE_ID` NUMBER REFERENCES `employees`(`EMPLOYEE_ID`),
  `START_DATE` TIME,
  `END_DATE` TIME,
  `JOB_ID` TEXT REFERENCES `jobs`(`JOB_ID`),
  `DEPARTMENT_ID` NUMBER REFERENCES `departments`(`DEPARTMENT_ID`),
  PRIMARY KEY (`EMPLOYEE_ID`)
);

CREATE TABLE `locations` (
  `LOCATION_ID` NUMBER,
  `STREET_ADDRESS` TEXT,
  `POSTAL_CODE` TEXT,
  `CITY` TEXT,
  `STATE_PROVINCE` TEXT,
  `COUNTRY_ID` TEXT REFERENCES `countries`(`COUNTRY_ID`),
  PRIMARY KEY (`LOCATION_ID`)
);

Question:
What is the average salary for each job title?
answer: SELECT job_title ,  AVG(salary) FROM employees AS T1 JOIN jobs AS T2 ON T1.job_id  =  T2.job_id GROUP BY T2.job_title

answer: SELECT name_first ,  name_last FROM player AS T1 JOIN all_star AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id WHERE YEAR  =  1998

answer: SELECT T1.name_first , T1.name_last ,  T1.player_id ,   count(*) FROM player AS T1 JOIN all_star AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id GROUP BY T1.player_id ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1;

answer: SELECT T2.team_id ,  T2.rank FROM home_game AS T1 JOIN team AS T2 ON T1.team_id  =  T2.team_id WHERE T1.year  =  2014 GROUP BY T1.team_id ORDER BY avg(T1.attendance) DESC LIMIT 1;

answer: SELECT T1.name_first ,  T1.name_last ,  T1.player_id FROM player AS T1 JOIN player_award AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id GROUP BY T1.player_id ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 3;

Question:
For each year, return the year and the number of times the team Boston Red Stockings won in the postseasons.
answer: SELECT count(*) ,  T1.year FROM postseason AS T1 JOIN team AS T2 ON T1.team_id_winner  =  T2.team_id_br WHERE T2.name  =  'Boston Red Stockings' GROUP BY T1.year

Question:
What are the first name and last name of the players who were paid salary by team Washington Nationals in both 2005 and 2007?
answer: SELECT T2.name_first ,  T2.name_last FROM salary AS T1 JOIN player AS T2 ON T1.player_id = T2.player_id JOIN team AS T3 ON T3.team_id_br = T1.team_id WHERE T1.year = 2005 AND T3.name = 'Washington Nationals' INTERSECT SELECT T2.name_first , T2.name_last FROM salary AS T1 JOIN player AS T2 ON T1.player_id = T2.player_id JOIN team AS T3 ON T3.team_id_br = T1.team_id WHERE T1.year = 2007 AND T3.name = 'Washington Nationals'

Question:
Count the total number of games the team Boston Red Stockings attended from 1990 to 2000.
answer: SELECT sum(T1.games) FROM home_game AS T1 JOIN team AS T2 ON T1.team_id = T2.team_id_br WHERE T2.name = 'Boston Red Stockings' AND T1.year BETWEEN 1990 AND 2000;

);

Question:
Which students live in the city with code "NYC" and have class senator votes in the spring election cycle? Count the numbers.
answer: SELECT count(*) FROM STUDENT AS T1 JOIN VOTING_RECORD AS T2 ON T1.StuID  =  Class_Senator_Vote WHERE T1.city_code  =  "NYC" AND T2.Election_Cycle  =  "Spring"

metadata.question: Find the first and last name of students who are not in the largest major.

answer: SELECT fname ,  lname FROM student WHERE major != (SELECT major FROM student GROUP BY major ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1)

metadata.question: What is the first and last name of the students who are not in the largest major?

answer: SELECT count(*) ,  sex FROM student WHERE age  >  (SELECT avg(age) FROM student) GROUP BY sex

metadata.question: Find the number of students whose age is older than the average age for each gender.

answer: SELECT count(*) ,  sex FROM student WHERE age  >  (SELECT avg(age) FROM student) GROUP BY sex

metadata.question: How many students are older than average for each gender?

answer: SELECT avg(T1.age) ,  T3.dorm_name FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid  =  T2.stuid JOIN dorm AS T3 ON T3.dormid  =  T2.dormid GROUP BY T3.dorm_name

metadata.question: Find the average age of students living in each dorm and the name of dorm.

answer: SELECT avg(T1.age) ,  T3.dorm_name FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid  =  T2.stuid JOIN dorm AS T3 ON T3.dormid  =  T2.dormid GROUP BY T3.dorm_name

metadata.question: What is the average age for each dorm and what are the names of each dorm?

answer: SELECT count(*) ,  T1.dormid FROM dorm AS T1 JOIN has_amenity AS T2 ON T1.dormid  =  T2.dormid WHERE T1.student_capacity  >  100 GROUP BY T1.dormid

metadata.question: Find the number of amenities for each of the dorms that can accommodate more than 100 students.

answer: SELECT count(*) ,  T1.dormid FROM dorm AS T1 JOIN has_amenity AS T2 ON T1.dormid  =  T2.dormid WHERE T1.student_capacity  >  100 GROUP BY T1.dormid

metadata.question: For each dorm, how many amenities does it have?

answer: SELECT count(*) ,  T3.dorm_name FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid  =  T2.stuid JOIN dorm AS T3 ON T3.dormid  =  T2.dormid WHERE T1.age  >  20 GROUP BY T3.dorm_name

metadata.question: Find the number of students who is older than 20 in each dorm.

answer: SELECT count(*) ,  T3.dorm_name FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid  =  T2.stuid JOIN dorm AS T3 ON T3.dormid  =  T2.dormid WHERE T1.age  >  20 GROUP BY T3.dorm_name

metadata.question: How many students are older than 20 in each dorm?

answer: SELECT T1.fname FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid  =  T2.stuid JOIN dorm AS T3 ON T3.dormid  =  T2.dormid WHERE T3.dorm_name  =  'Smith Hall'

metadata.question: Find the first name of students who are living in the Smith Hall.

answer: SELECT T1.fname FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid  =  T2.stuid JOIN dorm AS T3 ON T3.dormid  =  T2.dormid WHERE T3.dorm_name  =  'Smith Hall'

metadata.question: What are the first names of all students in Smith Hall?

answer: SELECT avg(T1.age) FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid  =  T2.stuid JOIN dorm AS T3 ON T3.dormid  =  T2.dormid WHERE T3.student_capacity  =  (SELECT max(student_capacity) FROM dorm)

metadata.question: Find the average age of students who are living in the dorm with the largest capacity.

answer: SELECT avg(T1.age) FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid  =  T2.stuid JOIN dorm AS T3 ON T3.dormid  =  T2.dormid WHERE T3.student_capacity  =  (SELECT max(student_capacity) FROM dorm)

metadata.question: What is the average age of students who are living in the dorm with the largest capacity?

answer: SELECT count(*) FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid  =  T2.stuid JOIN dorm AS T3 ON T3.dormid  =  T2.dormid WHERE T3.gender  =  'M'

metadata.question: Find the total number of students living in the male dorm (with gender M).

answer: SELECT count(*) FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid  =  T2.stuid JOIN dorm AS T3 ON T3.dormid  =  T2.dormid WHERE T3.gender  =  'M'

metadata.question: What are the total number of students who are living in a male dorm?

answer: SELECT count(*) FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid  =  T2.stuid JOIN dorm AS T3 ON T3.dormid  =  T2.dormid WHERE T3.dorm_name  =  'Smith Hall' AND T1.sex  =  'F'

metadata.question: Find the number of female students (with F sex) living in Smith Hall

answer: SELECT count(*) FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid  =  T2.stuid JOIN dorm AS T3 ON T3.dormid  =  T2.dormid WHERE T3.dorm_name  =  'Smith Hall' AND T1.sex  =  'F'

metadata.question: How many female students live in Smith Hall?

answer: SELECT T3.amenity_name FROM dorm AS T1 JOIN has_amenity AS T2 ON T1.dormid  =  T2.dormid JOIN dorm_amenity AS T3 ON T2.amenid  =  T3.amenid WHERE T1.dorm_name  =  'Smith Hall'

metadata.question: Find the name of amenities Smith Hall dorm have.

answer: SELECT T3.amenity_name FROM dorm AS T1 JOIN has_amenity AS T2 ON T1.dormid  =  T2.dormid JOIN dorm_amenity AS T3 ON T2.amenid  =  T3.amenid WHERE T1.dorm_name  =  'Smith Hall'

metadata.question: What are the names of the amenities that Smith Hall has?

answer: SELECT T3.amenity_name FROM dorm AS T1 JOIN has_amenity AS T2 ON T1.dormid  =  T2.dormid JOIN dorm_amenity AS T3 ON T2.amenid  =  T3.amenid WHERE T1.dorm_name  =  'Smith Hall' ORDER BY T3.amenity_name

metadata.question: Find the name of amenities Smith Hall dorm have. ordered the results by amenity names.

answer: SELECT T3.amenity_name FROM dorm AS T1 JOIN has_amenity AS T2 ON T1.dormid  =  T2.dormid JOIN dorm_amenity AS T3 ON T2.amenid  =  T3.amenid WHERE T1.dorm_name  =  'Smith Hall' ORDER BY T3.amenity_name

metadata.question: What amenities does Smith Hall have in alphabetical order?

answer: SELECT T1.amenity_name FROM dorm_amenity AS T1 JOIN has_amenity AS T2 ON T1.amenid  =  T2.amenid GROUP BY T2.amenid ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1

metadata.question: Find the name of amenity that is most common in all dorms.

answer: SELECT T1.amenity_name FROM dorm_amenity AS T1 JOIN has_amenity AS T2 ON T1.amenid  =  T2.amenid GROUP BY T2.amenid ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1

metadata.question: What is the most common amenity in the dorms?

answer: SELECT T1.fname FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid  =  T2.stuid WHERE T2.dormid IN (SELECT T2.dormid FROM dorm AS T3 JOIN has_amenity AS T4 ON T3.dormid  =  T4.dormid JOIN dorm_amenity AS T5 ON T4.amenid  =  T5.amenid GROUP BY T3.dormid ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1)

metadata.question: Find the first name of students who are living in the dorm that has most number of amenities.

answer: SELECT T1.fname FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid  =  T2.stuid WHERE T2.dormid IN (SELECT T2.dormid FROM dorm AS T3 JOIN has_amenity AS T4 ON T3.dormid  =  T4.dormid JOIN dorm_amenity AS T5 ON T4.amenid  =  T5.amenid GROUP BY T3.dormid ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1)

metadata.question: What are the first names of all students who live in the dorm with the most amenities?

answer: SELECT T1.dorm_name ,  T1.student_capacity FROM dorm AS T1 JOIN has_amenity AS T2 ON T1.dormid  =  T2.dormid JOIN dorm_amenity AS T3 ON T2.amenid  =  T3.amenid GROUP BY T2.dormid ORDER BY count(*) LIMIT 1

metadata.question: Find the name and capacity of the dorm with least number of amenities.

answer: SELECT T1.dorm_name ,  T1.student_capacity FROM dorm AS T1 JOIN has_amenity AS T2 ON T1.dormid  =  T2.dormid JOIN dorm_amenity AS T3 ON T2.amenid  =  T3.amenid GROUP BY T2.dormid ORDER BY count(*) LIMIT 1

metadata.question: What is the name and capacity of the dorm with the fewest amount of amenities?

answer: SELECT dorm_name FROM dorm EXCEPT SELECT T1.dorm_name FROM dorm AS T1 JOIN has_amenity AS T2 ON T1.dormid  =  T2.dormid JOIN dorm_amenity AS T3 ON T2.amenid  =  T3.amenid WHERE T3.amenity_name  =  'TV Lounge'

metadata.question: Find the name of dorms that do not have amenity TV Lounge.

answer: SELECT dorm_name FROM dorm EXCEPT SELECT T1.dorm_name FROM dorm AS T1 JOIN has_amenity AS T2 ON T1.dormid  =  T2.dormid JOIN dorm_amenity AS T3 ON T2.amenid  =  T3.amenid WHERE T3.amenity_name  =  'TV Lounge'

metadata.question: What are the names of the dorm that does not have a TV Lounge?

answer: SELECT T1.fname ,  T1.lname FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid  =  T2.stuid WHERE T2.dormid IN (SELECT T3.dormid FROM has_amenity AS T3 JOIN dorm_amenity AS T4 ON T3.amenid  =  T4.amenid WHERE T4.amenity_name  =  'TV Lounge')

metadata.question: Find the first and last name of students who are living in the dorms that have amenity TV Lounge.

answer: SELECT T1.fname ,  T1.lname FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid  =  T2.stuid WHERE T2.dormid IN (SELECT T3.dormid FROM has_amenity AS T3 JOIN dorm_amenity AS T4 ON T3.amenid  =  T4.amenid WHERE T4.amenity_name  =  'TV Lounge')

metadata.question: What are the first and last names of all students who are living in a dorm with a TV Lounge?

answer: SELECT T1.fname ,  T1.age FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid  =  T2.stuid WHERE T2.dormid NOT IN (SELECT T3.dormid FROM has_amenity AS T3 JOIN dorm_amenity AS T4 ON T3.amenid  =  T4.amenid WHERE T4.amenity_name  =  'TV Lounge')

metadata.question: Find the first name and age of students who are living in the dorms that do not have amenity TV Lounge.

answer: SELECT T1.fname ,  T1.age FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid  =  T2.stuid WHERE T2.dormid NOT IN (SELECT T3.dormid FROM has_amenity AS T3 JOIN dorm_amenity AS T4 ON T3.amenid  =  T4.amenid WHERE T4.amenity_name  =  'TV Lounge')

metadata.question: What is the first name and age of every student who lives in a dorm with a TV Lounge?

answer: SELECT T3.amenity_name FROM dorm AS T1 JOIN has_amenity AS T2 ON T1.dormid  =  T2.dormid JOIN dorm_amenity AS T3 ON T2.amenid  =  T3.amenid JOIN lives_in AS T4 ON T4.dormid  =  T1.dormid JOIN student AS T5 ON T5.stuid  =  T4.stuid WHERE T5.lname  =  'Smith'

metadata.question: Find the name of amenities of the dorm where the student with last name Smith is living in.

answer: SELECT T3.amenity_name FROM dorm AS T1 JOIN has_amenity AS T2 ON T1.dormid  =  T2.dormid JOIN dorm_amenity AS T3 ON T2.amenid  =  T3.amenid JOIN lives_in AS T4 ON T4.dormid  =  T1.dormid JOIN student AS T5 ON T5.stuid  =  T4.stuid WHERE T5.lname  =  'Smith'

metadata.question: List all the scientists' names, their projects' names, and the hours worked by that scientist on each project, in alphabetical order of project name, and then scientist name.

answer: SELECT T1.Name ,  T3.Name ,  T3.Hours FROM Scientists AS T1 JOIN AssignedTo AS T2 ON T1.SSN = T2.Scientist JOIN Projects AS T3 ON T2.Project = T3.Code ORDER BY T3.Name ,  T1.Name

metadata.question: What are the names of each scientist, the names of the projects that they work on, and the hours for each of those projects, listed in alphabetical order by project name, then scientist name.

answer: SELECT T2.name ,  T3.name FROM assignedto AS T1 JOIN projects AS T2 ON T1.project  =  T2.code JOIN scientists AS T3 ON T1.scientist  =  T3.SSN WHERE T2.hours  =  (SELECT min(hours) FROM projects)

metadata.question: Find name of the project that needs the least amount of time to finish and the name of scientists who worked on it.

answer: SELECT T2.name ,  T3.name FROM assignedto AS T1 JOIN projects AS T2 ON T1.project  =  T2.code JOIN scientists AS T3 ON T1.scientist  =  T3.SSN WHERE T2.hours  =  (SELECT min(hours) FROM projects)

answer: SELECT T1.title ,  T3.book_title FROM movie AS T1 JOIN culture_company AS T2 ON T1.movie_id  =  T2.movie_id JOIN book_club AS T3 ON T3.book_club_id  =  T2.book_club_id WHERE T2.incorporated_in  =  'China'

Database Schema:
CREATE TABLE `book_club` (
  `book_club_id` NUMBER,
  `Year` NUMBER,
  `Author_or_Editor` TEXT,
  `Book_Title` TEXT,
  `Publisher` TEXT,
  `Category` TEXT,
  `Result` TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (`book_club_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `movie` (
  `movie_id` NUMBER,
  `Title` TEXT,
  `Year` NUMBER,
  `Director` TEXT,
  `Budget_million` NUMBER,
  `Gross_worldwide` NUMBER,
  PRIMARY KEY (`movie_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `culture_company` (
  `Company_name` TEXT,
  `Type` TEXT,
  `Incorporated_in` TEXT,
  `Group_Equity_Shareholding` NUMBER,
  `book_club_id` TEXT REFERENCES `book_club`(`book_club_id`),
  `movie_id` TEXT REFERENCES `movie`(`movie_id`),
  PRIMARY KEY (`Company_name`)
);
